speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether the Ministerial Statement made by the Deputy Prime Minister on 17 August 2020 in respect of the fifth set of COVID-19 support measures will be considered and debated in Parliament; and (b) whether the revised spending plan will need to be approved by Parliament.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance what is the basis for announcing the additional $8 billion financial measures on 17 August 2020 and whether Parliament will be able to seek clarification on the financial measures.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what is the reason for the recent Ministerial Statement on further support measures being delivered via a broadcast and not in Parliament; (b) whether this is permissible under parliamentary procedures; and (c) whether and when MPs will have the opportunity to debate the measures in the Ministerial Statement in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The COVID-19 pandemic continues to evolve at an unprecedented pace.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It has demanded swift and robust responses from the Government.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Government has been monitoring the economic conditions and having regular interactions and dialogues with citizens and business leaders.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The coverage of some key schemes, including the Jobs Support Scheme, was going to end in August.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Businesses were concerned if the support would be extended.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many jobs and businesses may be at stake if we did not announce our policy measures in time.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our businesses and workers have found this reassurance useful in their decision making.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The COVID-19 situation has affected the projected spending of some Ministries and projects.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For example, delays in major construction projects such as new MRT lines have decreased development expenditure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To meet changing needs, MOF reallocated unutilised funds from these areas to fund the extension of these measures.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: MOF briefed President and Members of the Council of Presidential Advisors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These will reflect how funds will be re-allocated across different Heads of Expenditure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Government is responding swiftly to a fast-evolving situation and will share its plans with the public in a timely and clear fashion, while ensuring full accountability for the use of public monies.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I noted in the latest Budget Estimates released on 17 August, the projection for revenue continues to come down.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, can I ask the Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister whether there are further scope to reallocate monies from the Development Expenditure to fund further spending for this current FY as well as the spending in the next few years.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Also, constitutionally, we need to balance our Budget in each term of Government.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I would like to ask how would the Government weigh the consideration of reallocating funds set aside for expenditures for Development Expenditures which is investment for the future as well, versus further draw down on the reserves.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Well, I thank Mr Liang Eng Hwa for pointing out our revenues are continuing to come down.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For this financial year, the main underutilisation comes from development spending caused by delays in construction, as workers were in the dormitories and were unable to continue their work.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But for future years we are now carefully revewing the timeline for many of the development projects.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, we must continue to budget very carefully, in reallocating revenues, monies from the Development Expenditure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And the reason why we are first using the Development route first instead of tapping on these reserves, is that we have underutilisation this year because of construction.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But going forward, as Mr Liang Eng Hwa has pointed out, our fiscal position will be challenging – revenues are coming down while some expenditures are continuing to go up and the situation continues to be very fluid.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We do not know how the COVID-19 pandemic situation will continue to play out, a point which I emphasised in my speech earlier on in the Debate.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: MOF will have to examine the various options very carefully but with the clear goal of enabling us to navigate through this very major crisis and to emerge stronger.
